FOREWORD

This Indian Standard which is identical with IS0 7206-3 : 1988 `Implants for surgery - Partial and total hip joint prostheses : Part 3 Determination of endurance properties of stemmed femoral components without application of torsion', issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ), was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on the recommendation of the Orthopaedic Instruments and Accessories Sectional Committee and approval of the Medical Equipment and Hospital Planning Division Council. The text of above mentioned IS0 standard has been approved as suitable for publication as Indian Standard without deviation. Certain conventions are however not identical to those used in the Indian Standards. Attention is particularly drawn to the following: a) b) Wherever the words `International Standard' should be read as `Indian Standard'. appear, referring to this standard, they the current

Comma ( , ) has been used as a decimal marker while in Indian practice is to use a point ( . ) as the decimal marker.

7.1

Procedure

Hold the head or neck of the test specimen by means of the gripping device (6.7) and position the specimen so that axis KL of the stem, as designated in figure 3, is inclined at an angle of loo to the vertical. An example of a technique that may be used for setting the specimen in the correct orientation is given

If this indication is given by the testing machine or the instrument, terminate the test. Examine the embedding medium and the specimen to determine whether the specimen has loosened in the embedding medium or yield of the specimen has occurred. 7.9 Continue the test until one of the following events occurs : a) b) yield or loosening, as described in 7.8; fracture of the specimen;

in annex B.
NOTE - It is essential that the neck of the prosthesis is not marked or damaged during this process because damage can affect the endurance properties. Damage to the head of the prosthesis should also be avoided as this can increase the friction between the head and the loading system during testing.

1

c) registration of completion of the chosen number of load cycles. In each case, record the number of cycles.

7.2 Embed the specimen in the embedding medium (5.2) in the holder (6.2) so that the upper surface of the medium is at, a distance of 80 mm * 2 mm vertically below the centre of the head of the prosthesis (point C as defined in IS0 7206-l). Take care not to mark or otherwise damage the stem.

9

Disposal of test specimens

specimens;

It is imperative that the prosthesis should not be used for clinical purposes after testing. Care should be exercised in the use of the specimen for further mechanical tests because the. loading regime may have altered the mechanical properties. In particular, it is recommended that the specimen is not used for further endurance testing. 0

7.8

Set thk testing machine or other instrument to givaan indication if the vertical or horizontal component of the specimen deflection exceeds a preset value approximately 25 % greater than the deflection occurring in the first minute of running at test load.
